task: Independently analyze nonreversible finite-state mixing and entropy mechanisms.
target: Persistent velocity lift of the cycle, with a sharp TV-versus-relative-entropy mixing separation.

interface.target_cost: expected number of events by time t is (1+1/n)t; no oracle or nonlocal position jumps
interface.comparison: rate-one symmetric nearest-neighbor cycle; same order position-motion rate

claims.statement: For n>=3, the chain is irreducible, uniform on 2n states is stationary, and detailed balance fails.
claims.proof_basis: balanced incoming/outgoing rates and directed motion edge with zero reverse rate

claims.statement: Fourier blocks have eigenvalues cos(theta)-1-1/n +/- sqrt(n^-2-sin(theta)^2); for sufficiently large n, the real-part gap is 1/n+1-cos(2pi/n)=Theta(1/n).
The additive-reversibilization gap is min{2/n,1-cos(2pi/n)}=Theta(n^-2), a factor Theta(n) below the nonreversible real-part gap.
For each fixed epsilon in (0,1), worst-start TV mixing time is Theta_epsilon(n).
claims.proof_basis: uniform P_{2n}(z,z')>=c/n minorization from exactly one/two flips and a uniform Skellam local-CLT lower bound; Omega(n) from bounded-speed support

claims.statement: For each fixed positive KL threshold epsilon, worst-start D(P_t(z,.)||pi) mixing time is Theta_epsilon(n log log n); for every fixed a in (0,1), the worst-start KL at t=a n log log n diverges.
claims.proof_basis: Doeblin entropy contraction for upper bound; no-flip event plus binary data processing for lower bound

claims.statement: At time ns, scaled position and velocity should converge to the rate-one telegraph process on the unit circle; its no-flip atom suggests a nontrivial TV profile and no cutoff.
claims.missing: A local limit theorem in total variation for the m>=1 flip-count components and a careful singular/absolutely-continuous decomposition. No cutoff conclusion is asserted.

claims.statement: The exact order-n-versus-n-loglog-n TV/KL separation may be a useful extension, but no novelty or priority conclusion is established.
claims.missing: Broader targeted prior-art review and original-paper proof comparison.
